source.note: Far deictic 'that (yonder)', stem *h₁eno-/*h₁ono-: Fortson §7.10 *eno- or *ono- (Hitt. ēni-, OCS onŭ; §16.33 Arm. -n, the 'over there' member of the three-way system; §7.29 Gk ekeĩnos < *e-ḱe-eno-); Handbook ch. 21 §5.1 Hitt. anna/i- < *éno-; Handbook ch. 82 (Slavic) §5.1 OCS distal onъ < *h₂en-o-; Beekes §15.2.1 and Mallory & Adams §24.2 *h₂en- (OCS onъ, Lith. anàs). Chosen over *h₂ew- (Beekes only, as a particle 'away'; Handbook ch. 111 §4.3 treats Iranian *au̯a- as a secondary PII formation). h₁ rather than h₂ because Hittite, which keeps h₂ as ḫ-, has none (anna/i-, ēni-); Fortson's vowel-initial *eno- gets h₁ by this table's convention. No book declines it: every cell follows demonstrative_so (see _derived).
